Reroll / Use Help Cards (Optional) 1.2.4 4. Complete an Objective or Take a Help Card 1.2.5 5. End of Turn 1.3 End of the Game 2 SOLO VARIANT 2.1 Penalty for Failed Attempts 2.2 End of the Game & Scoring 216 “Alea iacta est” (The die is cast) – 3 dice, 216 possible combinations. The game combines classic dice-rolling luck with strategic dice manipulation to fulfill objective cards. GAME COMPONENTS 70 Objective cards - There are always 4 public objectives on display, which you complete for points... and possibly bonuses! 30 Help cards - Earn one when you FAIL to complete an objective on your turn OR in lieu of bonus points when you DO complete an objective. 3 Dice - A maximum of 2 rolls is available per turn (an initial roll and an optional re-roll). GAMEPLAY On your turn: 1. Roll the Dice The player rolls all 3 dice . 2. Complete an Objective and Claim a Bonus (Optional) If you fulfill an objective without re-rolling or using any help cards, you can claim the point value of the card PLUS its bonus: additional points OR a help card. ~ To claim an objective card, the dice must match the requirements of the card exactly. ~ Points and bonuses are locate at the top left corner of the card. You may opt to keep rolling rather than complete an objective at this point. 3. Reroll / Use Help Cards (Optional) You may choose up to 3 dice to re-roll. You can also play as many help cards from your hand as you like to strategically manipulate the dice results. You can re-roll and/or use help cards in any order. This is your last chance! 4. Complete an Objective or Take a Help Card The final rolled result is compared with the face-up objective cards in the display. ~ If you fulfilled a card, earn its points. ~ If you didn't, take a help card. ~ Again you have the option to take a help card instead of claiming an objective. 5. End of Turn A new objective is added to the display if there were only 3. Play passes clockwise. End of the Game The game end is triggered as soon as a specific point value has been earned (100 points by default), then the other players have a final turn. The player with the highest total score wins the game. SOLO VARIANT The solo variant provides a virtual opponent (the AI). Instead of rolling dice, the AI automatically takes the LEAST valuable objective card from the center of the table and adds its points to its score. Penalty for Failed Attempts If you fail to fulfill an objective card on your turn, the AI receives a 2nd objective card from the current display as a penalty. End of the Game & Scoring The game immediately ends as soon as your OR the AI reach 100 points . If your score is higher than the AI's, you won! [Rating: 4/10] After 1 game on BGA: I like the approach of keeping things as simple as possible. Only three dice and a maximum of one reroll is a bold statement. With a dice game this simple and luck-driven, I expect it to play out really smoothly. Like Yahtzee, Pickomino, Can't Stop, Roll to the Top, Lure, and all the others. That wasn’t the case here. I have to scan the available goal cards, take the aid cards into account, and then make the mathematically optimal decision. That takes more effort than I find enjoyable.

[Rating: 4/10] Rolling dice and fulfilling goal cards. There are modifiers for the dice rolls but this game still has a high amount of luck. Luck with the dice rolls, the goal cards that come out, and the modifiers players get.

[Rating: 4.3/10] dice rolling and contract game help card will be awarded if not fulfilling a contract highly dependent on rolling luck and not much variation on game play  also low on player interaction

[Rating: 5/10] Roll three dice. If you can fulfil one of the 4 contracts in the open draft, score it. If you can’t, roll once more and if you miss, take a help card that allows you to do dice wibbles to help fulfil contracts later. That’s it. Your strategy? Roll well. There’s nothing interesting, and nothing to do on opponent turns. At least it goes quickly enough.
